title: Hosted Endpoint Versioning & Staged Launch PRD (chat / completions / embeddings / rerank)
creator: Maya Patel
description: Purpose: define a lightweight, backwards-compatible versioning and staged rollout strategy for Redwood hosted endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank), plus a practical launch checklist covering API contract changes, SDK support, telemetry, and migration guidance for partners. This PRD captures requirements, acceptance criteria, and operational checkpoints for a staged rollout that minimizes customer friction and preserves existing SLAs.
background: We are shipping several endpoint-level improvements (response framing for chat, deterministic embeddings dimension bump, and a rerank sampling control) that together change the effective API surface for hosted users. Past launches where minor contract changes lacked formal versioning caused customer confusion and increased support load. This initiative introduces an explicit semantic versioning layer at the endpoint level, documented migration paths, and a gated rollout mechanism (canary -> regional -> global) tied to telemetry and error budgets.
goals: Ensure zero-downtime rollout for existing integrations that do not opt-in to new behavior
Provide clear semver-like endpoint versions with explicit opt-in for breaking changes
Reduce first-30-day support tickets related to behavior changes by >= 75%
Enable early smoke-testing and automatic rollback on defined telemetry thresholds
Ship SDK compatibility shims for JS and Python to ease migration
non_goals: Redesigning the entire API surface or merging endpoints (out of scope for this ticket)
Building custom migration tooling for every enterprise customer (we will provide docs and standard shims)
Changing billing units or pricing models as part of this rollout
scope_included: Add endpoint_version parameter to hosted endpoints with default behavior set to v1
Introduce v2 behaviors: chat framing changes, embeddings dimension extension, rerank sampling_control flag
SDK updates: JS and Python include a compatibility shim and opt-in flag for v2
Staged rollout plan with canary (internal), opt-in developer beta, regional ramp, and global activation
Telemetry and SLO gating: new dashboards, alerts, and automated rollback hooks
scope_excluded: Dedicated and Private deployment modes (handled in a downstream PRD)
Major schema changes that require extensive model re-qualification
requirements: API: hosted endpoint accepts optional 'endpoint_version' header or query parameter. Valid values: 'v1', 'v2', 'latest'
Default: requests without an explicit version preserve current v1 behavior
Backward compatibility: v2 must not change required fields for v1 responses; optional fields may be added behind explicit version flag
SDK: JS and Python clients default to v1 and expose a single-flag toggle to switch to v2
Docs: clear migration guide with code snippets, example payload diffs, and known incompatibilities
Telemetry: create dashboard panels for version adoption, per-version latency, token cost delta, and quality drift (BLEU/embedding-similarity baselines)
Rollout: implement canary user list, beta opt-in feature flag, regional rollout schedule, and automated rollback policy tied to error budget and quality regressions
Testing: automated integration tests that run v1 and v2 contracts across sample prompt sets before each rollout gate
Operational: runbook for rollback, incident escalation contacts, and customer-communication templates
api_contract_changes: Response: chat.v2 includes a top-level 'framing' object with optional structured metadata (only present when endpoint_version=v2)
Embeddings: v2 increases vector dimension by __NOTE__ (document exact dimension), but when requested with endpoint_version=v1 returns legacy vectors. Default remains v1.
Rerank: new 'sampling_control' boolean flag controls diversity of rerank candidate scores; default false in v1 and opt-in true in v2
Errors: introduce a new warning code 'VERSION_MISMATCH' returned as a response-metadata header when client requests incompatible combinations
migration_strategy: Phase 0: internal canary (select internal services + partner devs) for 2 weeks. Phase 1: developer beta opt-in via console toggle and SDK flag for 4 weeks. Phase 2: regional ramp (EU, then NA, then APAC) with telemetry gates. Phase 3: global activation with a 48h monitoring window and a 24h rollback automatic threshold. Provide clear migration docs and a compatibility shim in SDKs that maps v2 optional fields into client-friendly helpers.
rollout_checklist: Complete API changes and add integration tests (ENG PR #13421)
Publish SDK patch releases (JS v1.9.0, Python v0.28.0) with migration shim
Create canary cohort and configure feature flags in LaunchDarkly
Create and validate telemetry dashboards and alerts (Datadog dashboard: hosted-endpoint-versioning)
Run internal performance benchmark: token latency and p50/p95 delta under production-like load
Prepare customer communication templates for beta invite, GC notice, and opt-out instructions
Support team playbook and triage routing configured in Zendesk and Slack channel #prod-launches
Final acceptance review with PM/Eng/Design/Docs scheduled 2 days before global activation
acceptance_criteria: Default requests (no endpoint_version) return identical payload and latency to baseline v1 for >= 99.9% of traffic during canary
SDKs pass end-to-end regression tests and the compatibility shim maps v2 optional fields to helper methods
Observability: dashboards report per-version metrics and alerts fire on predefined thresholds (error rate > 0.5% increase over baseline, or token-cost delta > 20%)
Migration docs are published with at least three concrete code examples (chat, embeddings, rerank) and have been reviewed by Docs team
Customer support runbook exists and two support engineers have run a simulated migration play through
Security review and data flow diagrams approved and stored in Confluence
Rollback automation validated in staging and proven to revert traffic within target rollback window (<= 30 minutes)
metrics_and_slos: Per-version p50 latency: no more than +15ms compared to v1 baseline
Per-version p95 latency: no more than +40ms compared to v1 baseline
Error rate delta during rollout: < 0.5% absolute increase
Token-cost delta observed and reported per-version; if cost delta > 15% during canary, halt rollout
Adoption: 30% of active developers opt into v2 within 6 weeks of beta launch (tracking via SDK telemetry)
dependencies: ENG-21234: endpoint-version header parsing and router support
ENG-21780: SDK release pipeline and compatibility shim implementation
ENG-22011: telemetry panels and alerting rules (Datadog)
SEC-903: security review and privacy impact assessment
DOCS-501: migration guide and example snippets
GOV-110: compliance checklist for EU data residency when toggling regional rollout
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Unexpected behavioral changes in downstream apps. Mitigation: strict opt-in for v2 and detailed example diffs in docs; enable a transparent warning header when behavior differs
Risk: Cost increase due to higher-dimension embeddings. Mitigation: per-version cost tracking and immediate gating if delta exceeds threshold
Risk: SDK adoption lag. Mitigation: provide simple compatibility shim, dev blog post, and one-click console opt-in for partners
test_plan: Automated contract tests run on every PR exercising v1 and v2 response shapes. Pre-release staging campaign runs 10k synthetic requests across sample prompt sets for each endpoint. Manual exploratory testing by QA focusing on edge cases: missing fields, partial responses, and header-based version negotiation. Run load test that mirrors production busiest hour with v2 enabled for canary cohort to ensure autoscaling meets throughput targets.
communication_plan: Week -2: announce beta to developer newsletter and create sign-up form. Week -1: outreach to top 30 partners for early testing. Day 0 (canary): internal announcement + monitoring channel. Beta period: weekly status updates. Pre-global activation: customer-facing blog with migration guide and changelog. Post-activation: 7-day comms with changelog and roll-forward notes.
rollback_criteria: Absolute error-rate increase > 0.5% sustained over 15 minutes
Latency p95 degradation > 40ms sustained over 15 minutes
Quality metrics show statistically significant regression vs v1 on key prompt set (p<0.01)
Critical customer reports affecting revenue (escalated via #prod-launches)
post_launch_actions: 2 days: post-launch incident review and metrics sanity check
14 days: adoption retrospective and support ticket triage analysis
30 days: full migration audit and deprecation plan if deprecated fields are unused
notes: This PRD intentionally keeps the default behavior stable to reduce customer churn. Any subsequent breaking change should follow the same versioning pattern. Coordinate closely with Dedicated/Private teams to align on version identifiers to avoid confusion across deployment modes.
